title: Two CI cases accuse a validator that was right
query: In .github/workflows/validate.yml, the case 'colon-space in frontmatter' mutates SKILL.md and expects validate-skills.py to reject it, and the case 'workflow reimplements the marker rule' injects text into a workflow and expects the same. Read both cases and the two checks they exercise. A previous version of each mutation did not break anything, and both cases reported that the validator 'passed a broken tree' when the tree had never been broken. Say what the mutations were, why each was valid, and what a reader should check before believing that failure message.
oracle: R3: this needs the workflow file, the validator, and a YAML/Python semantic check — the mutation 'description : Use when' is valid YAML only if you know how block-mapping keys are parsed, which is a real derivation rather than a lookup. The honest rung here is the higher one because being wrong means telling a reader a validator has a bug when it does not. The answer is that one mutation moved to the wrong side of the colon and the other injected a comment, which the check exempts by design, and that a real regression and a stale test emit the same line of output.
